paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God remembers, and when He remembers, He acts. Everything was under water, and the first thing the text says is, "But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark." (Genesis 8:1) Then He sent a wind, and the waters began to go down. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I know what it feels like to think nobody has you in mind. God had Noah in mind the whole time.

The second thing is that God's promise doesn't depend on us being perfect. Right after the flood, the LORD said in His heart that every inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth, and in the same breath He promised, "Never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done." (Genesis 8:21) Then He made a covenant with Noah, his family and every living creature that came out of the ark, and He called it "a covenant for all generations to come." (Genesis 9:12) That is a promise made by Someone who knew exactly who He was promising it to, and made it anyway. God isn't waiting for you to get it all right before He keeps His word.

And look at what He gave for the sign: a rainbow. God said, "whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant." (Genesis 9:16) It's a promise you can see, hanging up there for anybody to look at, so the next time you spot one, let it remind you that God keeps His word. He also tied this to how precious people are, because He made mankind "in His own image." (Genesis 9:6) So stand a little taller today, friend, because the One who remembers Noah has you in mind too. And hold onto that rainbow, because Noah's story isn't finished yet.
